## Analysis

**Volume is flat** (step_01): ~144–206 events per 5000-unit bin across the whole period — no burst that could manufacture an apparent shift.

**Partner sets pivot at t ≈ 15246**, with a half-window of 5000 on each side:

| node | before [10246,15246] | after [15246,20246] | overlap |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1389 | 139,441,788,901,969,1057,1444,1702,1840 | 39,306,337,585,955,977,1147,1181,1247,1387,1725,1734 | **0** |
| 1776 | 55,61,68,118,139,441,788,901,1444,1464,1702,1840 | 39,306,425,585,977,1008,1147,1181,1247,1725 | **0** |

Jaccard overlap = 0 for both members. Critically, the change is **shared**: the two members' "old" sets co-contain {139, 441, 788, 901, 1444, 1702, 1840} and their "new" sets co-contain {39, 306, 585, 977, 1147, 1181, 1247, 1725}. A coordinated swap of a common contact pool is not what gradual, independent background turnover produces (global repeat_ratio is only 0.159, step_02, so shared repeated partners are non-trivial).

**Confounder controls:** the group members are not merely hyper-popular hubs (step_03: uniform ~90–94 events, ~30–34 partners each; step_04 shows node 496 with 390 events dominating the same window, so the group is not driving raw volume), and their event counts are essentially unchanged before vs. after the pivot (step_01) — the turnover is in *identity*, not *amount*, of contacts.
